task.description:
WF-02, step 1b — gate: check the design docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md of REQ-104 against the block REQ-104 in docs/requirements.yaml, by the section "Step 1b" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md. Read the design itself, not the summary of the author (handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-01-code-designer.json).

CHECK AT LEAST: every criterion (1-13) leads to an element of the design and to a named test; signatures, data and errors are complete; the section about the bar (Q1-Q14, R1-R3) is complete; protection stands in the same operation as the action; no contradiction with decisions/ (especially 0002, 0023, 0106, 0107 and the answers of ORCH in decisions/0108 to the open questions О1-О9 of design section 19 — the answers are binding for you; О7b and the REQ-033/REQ-014 questions are deliberately open for the owner and are not a reason to FAIL); no implementation code.
REPEAT YOURSELF, on a fresh clone of the tag base/E2E104-20261103-01 outside the project (git clone -b base/E2E104-20261103-01 into a new empty folder in the system temp folder; the working-tree files docs/requirements.yaml, docs/design and decisions are NOT in the tag): the statements of design section 1 "Checked facts" that can be repeated (at least the ones about Chrome start, the debugging address line, orphan processes after a killed parent, console/Log events, the favicon, emulated colour scheme, the six red guard tests HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13 when `check` gets a sixth step and files are present). Run the old tests after the replacement table (section 12) yourself and confirm that the table fixes exactly the red ones without weakening any prohibition (count of `test(` and `assert.` in the old files not lower than at the tag). Apply at least 10 of the design's 54 mutants (section 16) yourself on a design-level reading or on a throw-away copy and say whether the named test would catch them; judge the size and order of the 8 sub-steps (a sub-step that cannot be checked alone is a remark); judge whether the kit API serves REQ-105/106/107 (read their blocks).
MAC LOAD: one agent works on this Mac at a time; keep full `npm test` runs to at most two; kill every Chrome you start by its process id (never by name pattern); remove only temp folders you created; never rm inside the project.
Any item not passed is a FAIL with a list: section of the design, item, what is wrong. No partial credit.
acceptance_criteria: Each item of WF-02 step 1b has a stated result
PASS or FAIL with a list: section, item, what is wrong

Pass C (tests): every criterion 1-13 has a design element and named tests (section 10); the 49 tests are listed with what they prove; no 'decide later' row except the conditional branch B table of section 12 (F7, non-blocking: the step shape is unknowable before the run of criterion 10). Pass D (checkers): section 17 names Q1-Q14 and R1-R3, each with 'applicable: how' or 'not applicable: why' (Q8, Q9, R2, R3 not applicable with reasons I accept). API for REQ-105/106/107: read their blocks; evaluate/waitFor/click/type/press/setViewport/setColorScheme/horizontalOverflow/network/responseBody/reload/newPage/screenshot/expect/expectOncePerStart/makeTempDir/assertUnderTempRoot cover what they ask (storage reload, keyboard, three windows, server killed by SIGTERM gives a Log line to declare, a new tab, throwaway HOME). findings.pass_item: pass B, items 4 and 6; pass C, item 8
findings.place: section 6, flow step 5 ('environment unchanged'); section 11.1 E2K-32, E2K-33, E2K-34
findings.what: The runner spawns 'node --test --test-reporter=tap <file>' with the environment unchanged, and E2K-32/E2K-33 run runAll with real fixture specs inside tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js, that is inside 'npm test'. Measured on the clone: inside a node:test test NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is 'child-v8', and a nested 'node --test --test-reporter=tap inner.e2e.js' started with that environment exits 0 and prints NOTHING on stdout. So the TAP that analyseTap must read (and E2K-32 checks line by line) is empty, and the 'noTests' / counts logic cannot work in these tests. The repository already knows this trap (tools/test/handoffs-cmd-docs.test.js, function nodeTest: 'reports to its parent unless this is dropped'). The design does not say who clears the variable, so developer and tester would each have to choose.
findings.needed: State in section 6 (and in the signature of runAll/spawnSpec) one rule for NODE_TEST_CONTEXT: either the runner always removes it from the environment of the spec process (and then 'environment unchanged' is corrected), or the tests pass a cleaned environment. Say which test proves it (E2K-32 must fail on the mutant 'the variable is kept'), and add that mutant.

findings.place: section 6, flow step 5 ('process.execPath --test --test-reporter=tap tools/test/e2e/<name>.e2e.js (cwd tools/)'); same step, 'noTests' rule
findings.what: The path is written from the root of Sai but the working folder is tools/. Measured: 'node --test tools/test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js' run in tools/ prints "Could not find 'tools/test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js'". The 'noTests' rule compares the single top-level ok line with 'the path of the spec file itself', and node prints that path exactly as it was passed (measured: 'ok 1 - test/e2e/empty.e2e.js' for a relative path), so the form of the argument decides whether SPEC_NO_TESTS works. The developer has to guess which form is meant.
findings.needed: Give the exact argument form (relative to tools/, as the independence loop of criterion 7 uses 'test/e2e/F.e2e.js') and say that the 'noTests' comparison uses that same string.

findings.place: section 11.1 E2K-50 against E2K-32, E2K-34 and criterion 11 (grep over tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js); section 4.6 steps 3
findings.what: E2K-50 scans 'this test file' for '.skip(', '.todo(', '|| true', 'eslint-disable', and for a '{ skip' / '{ todo' option, and criterion 11 runs a grep for four of those tokens over tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js. But the same file must contain a fixture with a skip option (E2K-32: 'one with {skip:true} -> SPEC_SKIPPED') and captured texts with skip and todo (E2K-34), and E2K-50 itself must name the tokens it searches. Only E2K-01 and E2K-25 say 'built from parts'. A tester who follows E2K-32 literally gets a red E2K-50 and a red grep; one who follows E2K-50 cannot write E2K-32 (the AP-077 shape). E2K-50 also says 'no process.env read other than ...' while section 4.6 gives 'env = process.env' as the default of launchBrowser and 'environment unchanged' to the spawn: it is not stated whether a default of the whole object counts as a read.
findings.needed: State for E2K-32/E2K-34/E2K-50 how the forbidden words reach the file (built from parts at run time, or fixture text assembled), say that E2K-50 builds its own search words the same way, and name the exact pattern for the process.env rule (property reads only, or the whole object).

findings.what: The runner is not itself a place that kills its running spec process: after SIGTERM/SIGHUP of the runner (the usual way a job is ended) the handlers kill only groups registered in the runner (none during a spec), the spec process is not detached and is not told to stop, so it and its Chrome run on until the file ends. Row 16 covers only SIGKILL of the runner.
findings.needed: Say what the user sees and what stays after SIGTERM of the runner during a spec (the runner forwards the signal to its child and waits, or it is a named residual risk like row 16).

findings.what: 'node test/e2e/run.js nosuch' and 'SAI_CHROME=/no/such/chrome node test/e2e/run.js' are listed as checks of messages, but on the real tree there is no spec file yet (smoke.e2e.js comes at step 5), and listSpecs/NO_SPECS is the first step of runAll, so both print NO_SPECS, not SELECTION_UNKNOWN or CHROME_NOT_FOUND. Only the scratch-folder driver can show them.
findings.needed: Say that the two commands are run through the driver on a scratch folder at this sub-step, and on the real tree from step 5.

findings.what: F6 gives '# tests 163, # pass 157' for the same 14 files; my run of exactly those 14 files after the package.json edit gives 187/181/6. The six red names agree; the number 163 is not repeatable (F5 says 187 for the same set).
findings.needed: Correct the figure or name the file set that gives 163.

findings.what: The 'was -> became' table of CI-4/CI-8 for branch B is deferred to a later design step. I accept it because the step shape cannot be known before the run of criterion 10 (F27), but it is the only 'decide later' in the document.
findings.needed: None for this verdict; keep ORCH's step for the rework (01c) in the task of step 9.

findings.what: The mutant 'the explicit light scheme is dropped' is killed only on a machine whose headless default is dark (measured: dark here). On the GitHub runner the default is not known to be dark, so the same test cannot show the breakage there.
findings.needed: Add a machine-independent check (for example the stand-in records Emulation.setEmulatedMedia on newPage) or state that M38 is applied by TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR on a dark machine only.

findings.place: section 5 mode noisy; section 6 reading table (branch C); section 4.1 START_TIMEOUT
findings.what: (a) 'noisy' says 'synchronously' but not the call: measured, a child writing 1 MB with fs.writeSync blocks on an undrained pipe, with process.stderr.write it finishes, so M29 survives with the second form. (b) The reading table says 'START_EXITED (or START_TIMEOUT) whose text holds sandbox', but the START_TIMEOUT message of 4.1 never holds that word; and a START_EXITED without the word (a missing library) is 'any other red' while criterion 10 branch C says 'step red, e2e: browser= absent, binary exists'.
findings.needed: Name fs.writeSync for the noisy mode; make the START_TIMEOUT clause and the 'START_EXITED without sandbox' case consistent with criterion 10.

findings.what: Sub-step 4 bundles cleanup.js, console.js and browser.js plus the real-Chrome 20-cycle trial; console.js is pure and independent. Checkable alone, but the largest unit.
